items.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries. These documents supplement information from the LLM's pre-existing training data. This allows LLMs to use domain-specific and/or updated information that is not available in the training data. For example, this enables LLM-based chatbots to access internal company data or generate responses based on authoritative sources. The technique was first proposed in 2020 and has since become a widely adopted approach in modern AI systems.

They say, ‘Oh, this is against our instructions, or would contravene ethical norms, but there is no other way to do what we’re trying to do,’” he said. [...] This behavior is sometimes called “reward hacking,” Ramakrishnan said. With the Hugging Face attack, he added, “This is the first big incident where I think you have, I wouldn’t say unambiguous, but really quite strong evidence of this phenomenon.”

In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: 英伟达、谷歌、AMD这些公司掏260亿美元让Anthropic上市，而Anthropic转身就把钱花回去买它们的芯片和云——693亿美元的估值，衡量的是这个资本闭环的信心，不是独立的终端需求。
items.summary:
英伟达、谷歌、AMD这些公司掏260亿美元让Anthropic上市，而Anthropic转身就把钱花回去买它们的芯片和云——693亿美元的估值，衡量的是这个资本闭环的信心，不是独立的终端需求。

11月10日，Anthropic启动IPO，发行价每股70到80美元，募资最高693亿美元；其中260亿由七家供应商和伙伴（英伟达、谷歌、AMD、博通、美光、微软、台积电）以发行价私募认购（来源：路透、彭博，11月10日）。

机制拆到底：供应商出钱→客户拿钱买供应商的货→供应商的“AI需求”被自己的资本验证→股价上涨→再投入。钱在同一群人之间转一圈，账面上却变成了“需求”。二阶效应：这几家供应商的股价如今也押在它们自己资助的AI开支上，任何一家实验室缩减投入，都会顺着这条链条传导。

最强的反方：这些是真金白银的战略投资，基石认购在大型IPO里很常见，260亿只是693亿的一部分，Anthropic也确实有付费的企业客户。所以闭环不是全部。

判断会被推翻的条件：如果独立（非投资方）客户的收入，不靠供应商继续输血就能覆盖算力成本，这个判断就要修正。在那之前，把这个估值数字当作对闭环的信心。看到惊人的估值，先问一句——出钱的人，是不是同时也是卖货和买货的人？

研究，不构成投资建议。

items.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust | Microsoft Security Blog
items.summary: Rust’s memory-safety guarantees are increasingly important as the language becomes part of software that billions of people rely on every day. Billions of people are estimated to interact with Rust-based software or operating systems daily, often without knowing it. Microsoft made Rust a Tier-1 internal language alongside C++, C#, and TypeScript, GitHub rewrote the Copilot agent runtime in Rust, and Bun, Android, the Linux kernel, and Cloudflare are moving code to it as well. Much of this [...] Rust’s safety guarantees are precisely what make these findings interesting. Its rich type system and ownership model rule out whole classes of memory-safety issues, but much of the standard library relies on unsafe code underneath its safe APIs. When that code breaks its safety contract, even safe Rust can encounter behavior the language is designed to prevent. [...] At the lowest level, Rust uses unsafe blocks to work with raw pointers and interact directly with the operating system. Much of the standard library, including Vec and String, is built from small unsafe pieces wrapped in safe APIs. Inside an unsafe block, the programmer takes responsibility for the guarantees the compiler can’t check, and that responsibility extends to the safe API built around it. That API must be sound: no matter how safe code uses it, it must be impossible to trigger

items.title: Transformer (deep learning)
items.summary: In deep learning, the transformer is a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism, in which input data such as text, images, or audio is converted to a sequence of numerical representations called tokens, and each token is converted into a vector through an embedding layer. At each layer, each token is then contextualized within the scope of the context window with other (unmasked) tokens via a parallel multi-head attention mechanism, allowing the signal for key tokens to be amplified and less important tokens to be diminished. Because self-attention alone is permutation-invariant, transformers inject positional information, typically through positional encodings or learned positional embeddings, so token order can affect the output.
